primitives.note: Living Vengeance converts Varus' bonus attack speed into bonus AD and AP (11% standard / 33% empowered) whenever the kill buff is active.
On-kill buff grants bonus attack speed (and via conversion, AD/AP) for 5-11s (standard) or the same duration empowered (30% AS) after a champion takedown.
Empowered Living Vengeance raises Varus' attack speed cap to 3.33.

Piercing Arrow channels up to 4s (effects cap at 1.25s), blocking Hail of Arrows/Chain of Corruption and disabling basic attacks/most actions during the channel; damage and Blight-detonation bonus scale continuously with charge time.

Piercing Arrow deals damage only on its recast (charge itself deals none, and can be auto-cancelled with a partial mana refund); Blighted Quiver's active is a separate recastable buff (arm/consume/auto-expire) with its own 1s recast cooldown.
Mana costs (50-70 for Q, 90 for E, 100 for R) can gate cast frequency across the 15s window; W is free.
Blighted Quiver's passive on-hit bonus magic damage triggers on every qualifying basic attack.
Blight stacks (0-3) are applied by autoattacks and by Chain of Corruption's root, refresh on reapplication, and are detonated by any Varus ability hit for bonus magic damage.
Blight-stack detonation damage scales with the target's maximum health per stack; Blighted Quiver's active scales with the target's missing health.
Blighted Quiver's active arms the next Piercing Arrow within 5.5s with bonus magic damage based on target missing health.
Consuming Blight stacks against a champion(-equivalent) target refunds remaining cooldown on Varus' basic abilities (13% per stack, up to 39%, boosted by Q charge time).
Hail of Arrows (0.5s delayed landing) and Chain of Corruption deal fixed rank/AD/AP-scaling damage on cast, on cooldown.
Hail of Arrows applies Grievous Wounds (40% reduced healing/regen) to the target; only matters for damage taken if the target self-heals, which a stationary dummy does not do.

needsBespoke.why: Every mechanic in Varus' kit -- the kill-triggered stat-converting buff, the charged/recast Q, the on-hit/consumable Blight-stack system with its missing-health and max-health scalings, the empowered-attack W active, the stack-consumption cooldown refund, and the plain-cast E/R -- is expressible as a combination of listed primitives (stat-conversion, timed-self-buff, attack-speed-interaction, charge-or-channel, recast-or-multipart, resource-budget, onhit-rider, target-stacks, conditional-damage, empowered-attack, cooldown-manipulation, plain-cast, target-debuff). Nothing requires a form change, pet, ammo system, or other bespoke logic.

proposal: Pre-cast Blighted Quiver's active (W) to arm it before the first Piercing Arrow.
Cast Chain of Corruption (R) as an opener (or as soon as it is up) for its flat magic damage and to rapidly apply 3 Blight stacks over ~1.75s.
Charge Piercing Arrow (Q) to the 1.25s effect cap and release, dealing maximized Q damage and detonating all current Blight stacks (boosted by the charge-time bonus and any armed W active bonus).
Cast Hail of Arrows (E) on cooldown for its physical damage, letting it consume any accumulated Blight stacks (including a second consumption ~0.3s later).
Auto-attack continuously in the gaps between ability casts/channels to keep applying and refreshing Blight stacks and to deal the W on-hit bonus magic damage.

Re-arm W's active before each subsequent Q cast, and repeat R > (auto-attacks) > full-charge Q > E on cooldown, using the cooldown refunds from stack consumption to fit in extra casts as the fight goes on.
questions: Should Piercing Arrow always be charged to the full 1.25s effect cap, or does the post-effect cooldown-start rule make a partial charge better for total damage/kill time given more frequent casts?

Can Varus actually land a basic attack during Piercing Arrow's channel (disabled for most of it) or between other ability casts, and how should attack timing be modeled around the channel-block window?
Does the simulator allow W's active to be reliably re-armed before every Q cast within its 1s internal recast/5.5s empower window, or does that impose an effective minimum spacing between Q casts?
Is opening with R (to front-load Blight stacks for a subsequent big Q detonation) actually better for total 15s damage than opening with Q, given R's much longer cooldown?
